name: Community Salmon Program Grants
summary: Twice-yearly grants for volunteer, community and Indigenous-led salmon habitat assessment, restoration and stewardship projects in British Columbia and the Yukon. The foundation pays up to half of project costs; the rest is matched by funds or in-kind work.

eligibility.rule: Be community-based and take place in B.C. or the Yukon
Include significant volunteer involvement, with exceptions for Indigenous or remote organizations
For stock assessment projects, show an innovative one-time investment, not ongoing operational funding

documents: Project budget with volunteer or community hours
Necessary permits and letters of support
Letters of support from stewardship organizations or industry groups
Final Report for previous CSP projects, if required

calls.label: Fall and spring intakes
calls.recurring: Fall intake opens early September with an October 15 deadline; spring intake opens early January with a February 15 deadline.

status.quote: Grant intakes occur twice a year in the spring and fall.

recurring.quote: The fall intake opens in early September, and the application deadline is October 15. The spring intake opens in early January, and the application deadline is February 15.

applicant_types.quote: Be led by a volunteer group, not-for-profit, school, or Indigenous government both at the time of application and during the grant period;

geography.quote: Be community-based and take place in B.C. or the Yukon;

window.quote: Grant intakes occur twice a year in the spring and fall.

co_finance_required.quote: PSF will pay up to 50% of the total value of each project, and the rest must be matched by other funds and in-kind donations or work.

effort.quote: Applications are assessed by a Technical Review Committee and Grants Committee comprising PSF staff, board members, community representatives and independent salmon experts.

eligibility.quote: Be community-based and take place in B.C. or the Yukon;
Include significant volunteer involvement, with some exceptions for Indigenous or remote organizations;
As of 2026, proposed stock assessment projects must clearly show that they represent an innovative, one-time investment-not a request for ongoing operational funding.

co_finance.quote: PSF will pay up to 50% of the total value of each project, and the rest must be matched by other funds and in-kind donations or work.

documents.quote: Include all necessary details and volunteer or community hours in the budget.

Have the necessary permits and letters of support from relevant agencies, Crown and First Nations governments, or landowners; and, Have letters of support from relevant stewardship organizations or industry groups, even if they are not involved in the project.
Submit the Final Report for any previous CSP projects if required.
